Nina: Heads-up — after the package.json tidy in the SDK release, a few downstream TS projects see weird import/typing breakages. Sample apps in CI show import errors + incorrect types resolution.

Leo: can you paste what changed?

Nina: minimal snippet that shipped: 
```json
{"main":"./dist/cjs/index.cjs.js","module":"./dist/esm/index.mjs","types":"./dist/index.d.ts","exports":{ ".":{"import":"./dist/esm/index.mjs","require":"./dist/cjs/index.cjs.js"},"./package.json":"./package.json"}}
```

Arjun: the exports map isn't obviously wrong, but a couple of subtle effects: 1) TS consumers using `paths` or older resolver strategies sometimes ignore `exports` and fallback to `types` location; 2) some bundlers call `import sdk from` and expect a default, while our ESM bundle only does named exports; 3) adding `./package.json` subpath can expose our package.json to tooling that tries to read `types` from there and ends up with path mismatches.

Leo: concrete repro: `samples/nextjs` uses `import SDK from '@redwood-inference/sdk'` and gets runtime: `The requested module '/node_modules/@redwood-inference/sdk' does not provide an export named 'default'`. Also `samples/ts-lib` sees VSCode show `Could not find a declaration file for module '@redwood-inference/sdk'` even though types exist.

Nina: CI Bot flagged both samples during the release smoke run.

CI Bot: sample/nextjs smoke failed: `TypeError: The requested module '/node_modules/@redwood-inference/sdk' does not provide an export named 'default'`. sample/ts-lib lint shows: `error TS7016: Could not find a declaration file for module '@redwood-inference/sdk'`.

Arjun: short fix options: 1) republish revert, 2) add a small interop entry that guarantees `export default`, 3) add a `types` export in the `exports` map for modern TS resolvers and add `typesVersions` for older TS. Example additions: 
```json
"exports":{
  ".":{
    "import":"./dist/esm/index.mjs",
    "require":"./dist/cjs/index.cjs.js",
    "types":"./dist/index.d.ts"
  }
},
"types":"./dist/index.d.ts",
"typesVersions":{"<4.5": {"*": ["dist/legacy-types/*"]}}
```

Leo: I vote for adding `types` into `exports` + a small interop ESM build that does `export {default} from './index.mjs'` or `import * as X from './index.mjs'; export default (X && X.default) || X;`. That lets consumers using `import default` succeed while keeping strict exports.

Nina: sounds good. Short-term: I'll cut a patch that adds the interop and `types` in exports so TS tooling picks up declarations. Longer-term: we should add a release CI step that runs TypeScript resolution checks and a Next.js smoke test.

Docs Bot: created docs PR covering recommended patterns for `exports` + `typesVersions` and examples for default vs named import shapes. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/499 :books:

Arjun: also add a checklist item to the SDK release workflow: "If you change exports/main/module, run: Node sample, Next sample, TS library sample, and Wrangler sample."

Nina: done — cutting v1.18.1 now with the interop entry and types in exports. Will monitor CI.

CI Bot: post-patch run shows nextjs + ts-lib samples passing in release pipeline. All green.

Leo: nice. After we stabilize, let's bake the interop step into the build pipeline so humans don't have to remember it.

Nina: agreed. I'll open follow-ups for build automation and the CI resolver matrix. Thanks all. :tada:
